baseline.name: Count uppercase characters
baseline.approach: Count uppercase letters and accept none, all, or exactly the first character.

why: The first two letters determine the permitted case of later letters, allowing rejection at the first conflict.
quantitative_comparison: Worst-case inspection remains n characters for both approaches. Earlier rejection can save suffix checks on some invalid words, but its frequency and elapsed benefit have not been measured.
tradeoffs: Assumes English letters and a valid terminated string; non-uppercase punctuation would be treated as lowercase. No universal superiority over an equally linear baseline is established.
evidence_basis: Static worst-case and early-exit comparison; no workload distribution or timing data.
